title: Lovett hits Ramsey and pulls a pistol
summary: Lovett and Herman punished Ramsey for snitching; Goodwin later saw him in Chicago, and Lovett tells how he drew a pistol at 18th and Vine.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Did you tell him what I did to Ramsey?
Tell us Baby, what you did to Ramsey.
After we found out he was snitching to the president about us working under scale, I hit him in the mouth.
And you weren't the only one; it was Herman too.

I hit him in the mouth because it was pretty tough back in those days and we weren't making any money and he snitched to the president about us working under scale and I asked him about it and he gave me did some big talk and I hit him in the mouth. That was all.
What ever happened to Ramsey, Baby, do you know.
I saw --
No.
Shall I answer that?
Yes.
All right Crook, what happened?
I saw Ramsey about eight years ago in Chicago. He lives in Chicago.
It wasn't when we were playing there? You didn't say anything.
No, it was before then, about two or three years before we went to play up there. I saw him at the DuSable Hotel, which doesn't exist anymore but I talked to him --
In the black side of town?
It was on the --
Southside?
-- Southside and I think it was on DuSable Boulevard but that's right on the Southside of Chicago and --
Tell us what happened?
-- I was in a club there and --
And what was he doing in there?
Just hanging around, and I talked to him, spoke to him. We never did bring up this occasion that he had done us wrong, you know, and took off like a big bird
you know, when the guys got after him. I mean, we run him for about half a block and if he hadn't been a good runner, boy, he would have got hurt.
Well, you remember when I laid that deal on him?
What was that, Baby?
I had a pistol that day and I was mad when I met him up on the corner of 18th and Vine -- 18th and Vine I met him up there, man.
What was this the next day or something?

No, about two or three days after that and I started to ask him -- I asked him why did he do that, you know, to us because I said, 'You were hungry and we were hungry too' and he gave me some big talk so I hit him and then -- I hate to say this but I had a pistol and I pulled the pistol on him, man, he went running down the street so I just let the pistol fall like that. I couldn't shoot him but he was running away from me, you know.
He really got you fellows upset. Well this was your bread and butter --
Oh man, life's blood.
Life blood, right.
Back in those days we weren't making nothing no way.
But you had to live on what you were
making.
Yeah, and then working with a man who would go and snitch to the president.
We had bought his uniform for him --
Yeah.
-- and everything like this, you know, and he didn't have to pay for that uniform. He had to stoop pretty low to go into something like this.
